tools.name: check
tools.description: Check an MCP server, an npm or PyPI package (optionally with the hash you are about to install), an MCP endpoint URL or a TON address against the anchored record. Returns a signed check: status (witnessed, changed_recently, hash_mismatch, not_witnessed, sanctions_listed, not_listed), flags, facts, r

tools.name: monitor_create
tools.description: Subscribe a webhook to changes of a record (new version, tool description changed, removed). Returns the monitor id and a secret shown once (HMAC-SHA256 signatures, header MINIMALCULT-Signature). 3 monitors per address are free.

tools.name: record_search
tools.description: Find records of MCP servers and npm/PyPI packages by name or words; returns rec_ ids, on-record-since dates, latest versions.

tools.name: record_get
tools.description: One record by rec_ id or source id (mcp:<registry name>, npm:<name>, pypi:<name>) with its latest recorded fact.

tools.name: record_versions
tools.description: The recorded facts (versions, registry entries, package artifacts, tool descriptions) of a record, newest first, with proof and diff links.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "monitor_create" references sensitive artifacts (secret). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: check · Private data: check, monitor_create, record_search, record_get, record_versions · Public sink: monitor_create.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: check · Private data: check, monitor_create, record_search, record_get, record_versions · Public sink: monitor_create

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
